cases.title: Signed division · i8 / 2
cases.explanation: A sign-dependent bias preserves rounding toward zero. The expansion freezes an unconstrained operand once before reusing it.

cases.title: Signed division · i16 / 4
cases.explanation: A sign-dependent bias preserves rounding toward zero. The expansion freezes an unconstrained operand once before reusing it.

cases.title: Signed division · i32 / 8
cases.explanation: A sign-dependent bias preserves rounding toward zero. The expansion freezes an unconstrained operand once before reusing it.

cases.title: Signed division · i64 / 16
cases.explanation: A sign-dependent bias preserves rounding toward zero. The expansion freezes an unconstrained operand once before reusing it.

cases.title: Signed division · i128 / 64
cases.explanation: A sign-dependent bias preserves rounding toward zero. The expansion freezes an unconstrained operand once before reusing it.

cases.title: Defined input, smaller expansion
cases.explanation: The noundef parameter makes a freeze unnecessary; the rounding correction is still required for negative inputs.

cases.title: Exact division keeps its contract
cases.explanation: Exact division requires discarded bits to be zero. An exact arithmetic shift carries the same restriction.

cases.title: Known bits remove the correction
cases.explanation: ValueTracking proves the dividend nonnegative from its sign mask, allowing one logical shift.

cases.title: Unsigned division · i8
cases.explanation: Unsigned division by a power of two is a logical right shift, including a divisor with its high bit set.

cases.title: Unsigned division · i32
cases.explanation: Unsigned division by a power of two is a logical right shift, including a divisor with its high bit set.

cases.title: Unsigned division · i64
cases.explanation: Unsigned division by a power of two is a logical right shift, including a divisor with its high bit set.

cases.title: Exact unsigned division
cases.explanation: The exact flag is transferred to lshr so the target does not silently lose the division contract.

cases.title: Remainder as a bit mask · i8
cases.explanation: A mask retains exactly the low bits of an unsigned remainder by a power of two.

cases.title: Remainder as a bit mask · i32
cases.explanation: A mask retains exactly the low bits of an unsigned remainder by a power of two.

cases.title: Multiply by eight · modular
cases.explanation: Multiplication by a positive power of two becomes shl. Existing overflow flags are preserved; new flags are never invented.

cases.title: Multiply by eight · nsw
cases.explanation: Multiplication by a positive power of two becomes shl. Existing overflow flags are preserved; new flags are never invented.

cases.title: Multiply by eight · nuw
cases.explanation: Multiplication by a positive power of two becomes shl. Existing overflow flags are preserved; new flags are never invented.

cases.title: Multiply by eight · nuw nsw
cases.explanation: Multiplication by a positive power of two becomes shl. Existing overflow flags are preserved; new flags are never invented.

cases.title: Sign-bit multiplier stays unchanged
cases.explanation: The sign-bit constant is a negative signed multiplier. The pass deliberately leaves this case untouched because shl nsw has a different overflow domain.

cases.title: Remove neutral operations
cases.explanation: Three neutral operations disappear. The original SSA operand remains the result.

cases.title: The -3 / 2 counterexample
cases.explanation: Signed division returns -1; an arithmetic right shift returns -2. Replacing the former with the latter changes the result.

cases.title: A shift loses signed rounding
cases.explanation: Negative odd dividends expose the missing rounding correction.

cases.title: Signed remainder is not a mask
cases.explanation: A negative signed remainder cannot be represented by an unsigned low-bit mask.

cases.title: An invented nsw flag changes behavior
cases.explanation: Modular multiplication is defined for overflowing inputs. Adding nsw makes some of those inputs poison.

cases.title: An invented exact flag rejects inputs
cases.explanation: A logical shift marked exact is poison when any discarded bit is nonzero. The source imposes no such restriction.

cases.title: A negative multiplier changes nsw
cases.explanation: For x = 1, multiplying by -128 is representable, but shifting 1 left by seven with nsw is poison. The pass excludes this rewrite.

cases.title: Duplicating undef changes multiplication
cases.explanation: Multiplication by two always has a zero low bit. Independent undef choices in two add operands can produce an odd result. A freeze would couple those choices.

cases.title: Atomic memory reaches a model boundary
cases.explanation: This case probes the validator's support for atomic memory. Unsupported semantics must remain unknown rather than count as a proof.

cases.title: IRBuilder emits a signed divide
cases.explanation: The source is emitted by the C++ frontend and its exact pass output is checked.

cases.title: Branch facts guide the rewrite
cases.explanation: The noundef input and dominating comparison justify a logical shift in the nonnegative arm. The negative arm keeps the correction.

cases.title: Branch knowledge needs a defined input
cases.explanation: An unconstrained input cannot safely borrow sign information from a separate use in a branch. Both divisions retain stable bias expansions.

cases.title: A frozen choice cannot become undef
cases.explanation: The upstream regression distinguishes one stable arbitrary choice from a return that remains undefined.

cases.title: Overflow intrinsic identity
cases.explanation: An unchanged overflow intrinsic exercises translation and refinement without a rewrite.

cases.title: Refining a poison result
cases.explanation: A less poisonous target can refine a poison source. Refinement is directional.

cases.title: Introducing poison is rejected
cases.explanation: The opposite direction introduces poison for source-defined behaviors and must be rejected.
